the_work: Caption Facebook and Instagram, TikTok script, blog article for search, product description for each marketplace listing, and the same message rewritten per platform
can_be_bought: Yes, freelance per article or per caption batch; quality varies with whether a brief exists, which is the input the buyer usually does not have
slips_when_busy: Never. The empty page is the one failure the owner sees the same day
what_breaks_if_dropped: Nothing this week, which is why it is never dropped and always written last, from nothing, at speed

the_work: Post images, marketplace banners, thumbnails, key visual, price tags, standee, and every one of them resized for four placements
commands: compose; scale; colour; identify; produce; adapt
can_be_bought: Yes, freelance per asset or a template pack; a template pack shifts the cost from making the asset to deciding what goes in it, which is the part that was hard
slips_when_busy: No. A post cannot go out without an image, so this gets done badly rather than late, and the palette is chosen in the last ten minutes
what_breaks_if_dropped: Consistency first, then recognition. Nobody notices for a quarter

the_work: Shoot the product on a phone, on whatever surface is in the office, generate the scenes that could not be built in the office, then get twelve usable frames out of the two that came out
can_be_bought: Yes, a packshot studio per SKU. This is the role most worth buying, because the output is reusable for a year and the skill gap is largest
slips_when_busy: Yes. Last year's photo gets reused, which is why the feed looks identical in January and September
what_breaks_if_dropped: Every downstream asset inherits one tired photograph, and no amount of layout recovers a frame with the wrong light in it

the_work: Shoot Reels and TikTok on a phone, cut in CapCut, burn in subtitles, cut the same footage again at a second aspect ratio and a shorter length
can_be_bought: Yes, freelance editing per video; the shooting is harder to buy because it needs the product in the room
slips_when_busy: No on TikTok, where the algorithm punishes a gap. Yes everywhere else
what_breaks_if_dropped: Short-form reach, which for a Vietnamese SME is now the cheapest reach available and the hardest to substitute

the_work: Answer every inbox and comment, run the Zalo and Facebook group, seed replies, handle a bad review in public, and do all of it inside the response window the platform measures
artifact_per_cycle: none - no command in the surface covers it, because it produces no artefact. That is exactly why it is invisible in every plan and why it consumes the day
can_be_bought: Partly. Scripted replies can be delegated; a bad review in public cannot
slips_when_busy: Never. An unanswered inbox is a lost order, so this interrupts everything else and cannot be batched
what_breaks_if_dropped: Revenue, immediately and visibly. This is the role that wins the argument about priorities and should

the_work: Facebook and TikTok campaigns, marketplace ads, daily budget, creative rotation, and reconciling what was spent against what the platform reported
can_be_bought: Yes, agency or freelance, usually on a share of spend. That fee structure rewards spending more, which is a conflict to price in rather than pretend away
slips_when_busy: No. Money leaves the account whether or not anyone is watching it
what_breaks_if_dropped: Spend continues into a creative nobody rotated and an audience nobody chose

the_work: Listings on Shopee, Lazada and TikTok Shop, product titles written for the platform's own search, voucher and flash-sale registration, and the double-date campaign calendar the platform sets and does not negotiate
can_be_bought: Yes, an operations service exists for exactly this; it is the least glamorous and most reliably worthwhile thing to outsource
slips_when_busy: No. Registration windows close and the discount funding is lost
what_breaks_if_dropped: The campaign the platform was going to subsidise runs without you, and the traffic goes to a competitor who registered on time

the_work: Find creators, negotiate, brief, ship samples, chase the post, reconcile payment, and secure the right to reuse the content in paid media
can_be_bought: Yes, booking agencies and platforms. What they do not supply is the brief
slips_when_busy: The booking never slips. The usage right and the brief both do
what_breaks_if_dropped: Content that cannot legally be boosted, which is the whole reason the budget was approved

the_work: Send print files, argue about colour, check a proof, approve labels, boxes, bags and standees, and catch the error before the run rather than after
can_be_bought: The prepress can be bought. The approval cannot: the person who signs off the proof owns the wasted run
slips_when_busy: Yes, until a proof is signed off unread and ten thousand boxes are wrong
what_breaks_if_dropped: A whole print run, in one payment, with no partial recovery

the_work: Copy numbers out of four platforms into one spreadsheet every week, and present it to an owner who wants to know whether it is working
can_be_bought: The collection can be automated. The diagnosis cannot be bought from someone who was not in the room when the decisions were made
slips_when_busy: The report never slips because it is asked for. The diagnosis always slips, because nobody asks for it by name
what_breaks_if_dropped: Nothing visible. The numbers keep arriving and stop changing anything, which is the most expensive failure in this table and the quietest

role_vi: Hỗ trợ bán hàng và chốt đơn
the_work: Chase orders, follow up leads, handle returns and exchanges, and cover the phone. None of it is marketing. It lands here because the marketer is the person at the desk with the customer's message already open
artifact_per_cycle: none - and no command in the surface covers it, which is the point of the row: it consumes marketing capacity and produces no marketing artefact
can_be_bought: Yes, and it is the single highest-value hour to hand to somebody else, because it competes directly with every other row here
what_breaks_if_dropped: Nothing in marketing. Name it, measure it, and move it, because until it is named it is invisible in every capacity conversation

the_work: Trade fair, sampling booth, store opening, sponsor deliverables, and the logistics of getting product and people to a fixed date
can_be_bought: Yes, event agencies. The brief and the on-site decisions stay in-house
slips_when_busy: No. The date is fixed and it absorbs whatever week it lands in
what_breaks_if_dropped: A committed date with an incomplete booth, in public

filed_under: Nhân viên Marketing - and this is the part of the title everyone believes they were hired for
the_work: Choose the buyer, choose the promise, choose what not to sell, choose the price position, and write it down where the other twelve roles can read it
commands: brainstorm; research; investigate; survey; segment; position; offer
can_be_bought: Consultancies sell it. What cannot be bought is the decision, and a bought document nobody in the building agreed with changes no caption
slips_when_busy: Always, and first. It has no deadline, no visible output this week, and nobody in the company asks for it by name
what_breaks_if_dropped: Every other row starts guessing. Ads optimise toward a buyer nobody chose, content is written to nobody, the palette is picked on taste, and the weekly report measures activity because there is no chosen outcome to measure against
